messages:
jin: FYI I've reorganized the az6 provisioning playbook into a smaller stepwise checklist and added a "Known Issues" section. Please skim and flag anything missing.

maria: Link?

jin: /playbooks/az6/provisioning (doc ref pasted in console) — top-level changes: 1) split network prep from node bootstrap; 2) separate GPU driver + CUDA step; 3) validation scripts + sample outputs.

alex: Nice. Can you paste the quick validation commands here so oncall can run without opening the doc?

jin: Sure. Quick kube + GPU checks:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl describe node <node> | egrep -i 'gpu|allocatable'
# nvml health (runs on node):
sudo /opt/nvidia/bin/nvidia-smi -q | head -n 20
# driver vs cuda check
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
```

sam: Adding a small note: we've seen az6 hosts on 100G NICs require MTU 9000 for RDMA tests to pass. Is that documented?

jin: Good catch — added under network prep: "If using RDMA NICs, set MTU=9000 on host and CNI; check path MTU to your fabric switches."

maria: Known issues I skimmed: one about kubelet panics when GPU driver mismatches kernel ABI. Can we add a remediation step (rollback to previous driver + cordon)?

jin: Done. Remediation item: cordon node, drain with --ignore-daemonsets, install matching driver from internal driver repo, reboot, uncordon.

alex: Also put in the emergency fallback: if whole AZ starts failing autoscaling, route traffic to fallback region via router policy. We had an incident once where az6 preemptions spiked.

jin: Added fallback routing snippet and policy id used by traffic-router. Note: this isn't automatic; ops needs to enable via console.

sam: Cost item — can we document recommended mix of reserved vs spot for Dedicated pools? Especially for model-inference vs batch workloads.

jin: Added a short table: inference = 80% reserved + 20% spot (min spot eviction tolerance), batch = 40% reserved + 60% spot. Also added an example pricing calc and per-token cost impact note.

maria: Small nit: the kubelet extra args config sample uses deprecated flags in 1.28. Please update to config file snippet rather than flags.

jin: Updated kubelet config section to use /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml example.

alex: One more operational note: CVE tracking — tag nodes with label infra.sec/patch-window to control rolling windows for kernel upgrades.

jin: Added label recommendation and example command:
```bash
kubectl label node <node> infra.sec/patch-window=2026-03-20-02:00-04:00
```

sre-bot: Reminder — az6 GPU quota request (ticket #4567) moved to Approved; provisioning window opens 2026-03-22 00:00 UTC.

maria: Great. Who owns final handoff?

jin: I'm marking sam as runbook owner for az6. Sam, please do a quick dry-run with the playbook on a staging subset next week.

sam: Will do. I'll run through: network prep -> driver install -> kube node join -> GPU validation -> workload sanity (small perf job) -> health dashboard check. Any specific perf job?

jin: Use perf-kit micro-benchmarks: small 2-node inference load with 1k concurrent tokens for 5 minutes. Add conformance check: p95 latency < 250ms for the tiny model.

alex: Noted. Also, known flaky issue we added: NFS mounts with NFSv4 locking can cause kubelet start delays — workaround: switch to async mounts or pre-create mountpoint and prefetch.

maria: Put the exact log lines in Known Issues so oncall can grep quickly.

jin: Done. Example grep: `journalctl -u kubelet | grep -i "nfs.*failed to mount"` and added sample log snippet.

sam: Thanks. I'll run the dry-run Tuesday and post a short thread with outputs. If we see anything blocking, I'll open an ops incident.

jin: Thanks team. If no objections I'll cut the doc as v1.1 at EOD and notify Solutions and SRE. :thumbsup:

alex: :thumbsup:

maria: LGTM

sre-bot: playbook/az6/provisioning version 1.1 published by jin at 1764123599
